fitReason: Strong CS/AI and physical-robot fit in uncertain marine environments: learned depth, visual representations, multimodal estimation and active autonomous exploration. The official joint graduate-program faculty roster and current lab graduate-student roster establish an academic mentoring role. The actual host is WHOI in Woods Hole, Massachusetts; this is not an MIT campus appointment.

physicalEvidence.summary: ReefMapGS (April 2026) uses actual CUREE autonomous reef surveys with camera, DVL, IMU and pressure sensors, covering 347.3 m and 695.5 m. It combines learned depth/uncertainty with 3DGS and factor-graph pose refinement; evaluation is workstation-based, not evidence of the entire pipeline controlling the AUV onboard in real time. A separate July 2026 lab report for its Science Robotics study documents autonomous acoustic-visual hotspot seeking in the Caribbean. The May 13, 2026 WHOI release dates the hotspot expeditions to 2022–2024 and names Girdhar as project PI; the 2026 article/report dates must not be read as new 2026 expeditions.

name: Nare Karapetyan
school: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI); MIT-WHOI Joint Program
title: WHOI Assistant Scientist I; MIT-WHOI Joint Program faculty
department: Applied Ocean Physics and Engineering; FIeld robotics and aLgorithmic Decision-making (FILD) Lab
fitReason: Substantive embodied-AI methods for marine robot perception, information gathering and vision-language planning. Current official joint-program faculty membership supports academic mentor scope. The lab is based at WHOI in Woods Hole, Massachusetts; no MIT campus hosting appointment is implied.

physicalEvidence.summary: The February 2026 revision of DREAM, coauthored by Karapetyan, verifies a real BlueROV2 surveying 200 oyster shells and two pipes in a controlled tank, with visual segmentation and GPT-5-based high-level planning feeding a classical PD/IMU-DVL state-estimation stack. The main quantitative coverage and efficiency results are from Oystersim; the actual tank run is a qualitative feasibility demonstration, not an open-ocean mission or quantified hardware success rate. The manuscript gives inconsistent tank-diameter descriptions, so no single exact diameter is adopted. This is collaborative hardware evidence involving USF/UMD/WHOI/Delaware; no current FILD ownership or visitor access to that specific BlueROV2 is established. Separately, the March 2026 DINOv2 environmental-context search paper uses actual AUV imagery but explicitly simulates robot motion offline, so it is not counted as learned live execution.
